root_idea.summary: The root has two prominent orientations: yellow or dark coloration and emptiness or vacancy. Classical Arabic also develops distinct branches for brass or copper, whistling, a month or season, and various plants.
root_idea.development: The lexical sources present these as differentiated branches rather than one single derivational sequence. The Quranic forms center on color and becoming yellow; emptiness, metal, sound, seasonal, medical, and botanical uses remain separate lexical developments.

qac_form_accounting.reason: Displayed under the normalized feminine adjective citation form.
Displayed under the singular adjective citation form أَصْفَرُ; the supplied Quranic form صُفْرٌ is its plural form and also admits a metal-noun interpretation in the cited Quranic expression.
Displayed under the active-participial citation form مُصْفَرّ.

senses.definition: Yellow; a color term lying between black and white.
senses.usage_conditions: Feminine adjective. In the description of the cow in 2:69, the ordinary reading is yellow and intensely bright.

senses.definition: Dark or black, as an extended interpretation of the color term.
senses.usage_conditions: A reported interpretation of صَفْرَاءُ in 2:69 takes it as black or dark; this interpretation is disputed, and is not the unqualified ordinary meaning of the adjective.
The Quranic form is the plural صُفْرٌ. In 77:33 it describes camels or camel-like forms, while the adjective itself is not restricted to that class of object.

senses.definition: Black or dark with yellow hairs intermingled.
senses.usage_conditions: In the Quranic expression of 77:33, the color term is explicitly explained as applying to a black or dark ground color containing yellow hairs; this is a camel-specific contextual coloration, not a general replacement for yellow.

senses.definition: Yellow metal, especially brass or copper.
senses.usage_conditions: An alternative Quranic interpretation of صُفْرٌ in 77:33 understands it as the metal extracted from minerals rather than as the plural adjective أَصْفَرٌ.

senses.definition: Turned yellow; becoming or having become yellow.
senses.usage_conditions: An active participial form describing a thing in the state or process of becoming yellow, including the vegetation described in the Quranic contexts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To whistle or utter a sound without articulated letters; of a bird, serpent, or person.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Also used of whistling into a whistle or calling an ass to water by whistling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become empty, void, or vacant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a house, tent, vessel, skin, hand, or other thing; figuratively, the emptying of a person’s vessels or property can mean that he died or perished.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To suffer from ṣufār, the disease involving yellow fluid in the abdomen.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The verb is explained through the medical noun صُفَارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To make yellow; to dye something yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied especially to a garment or piece of cloth.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To empty or make void, especially to deprive a house, tent, or yard of its contents or property.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The causative expression may refer to taking away livestock or property so that the household or yard is left without them.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become poor.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Said of a person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of cattle, to come into good condition or become fat after the intense summer heat has passed.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The usage is associated with the seasonal period called الصَّفَرِيَّة.

other_classical_meanings.definition: To become black as well as to become yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The source distinguishes a more constant state from a transient one in related forms; this is a broader Classical usage, not an additional Quranic meaning of مُصْفَرّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Empty, void, vacant, or devoid of contents; empty-handed or devoid of good.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Applied to houses, tents, vessels, hands, people, and things. The same adjective can be used in idiomatic expressions for total emptiness.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Zero or nought in the Indian system of arithmetic notation.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A technical use of the noun for the sign denoting nothing.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gold, gold coins or dinars, and women’s gold ornaments.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The applications are explained either through their yellow color or through resemblance to the metal called صُفْرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A state of madness in which a person’s reason fails.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The idiom لَفِي صُفْرِهِ is connected with the former practice of rubbing such a person with saffron.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hunger or a bout of hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominal use of the verbal noun associated with becoming empty.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease of the belly involving a collection of water and causing the face to become yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This medical meaning is distinguished from the related belief in a serpent or worms in the belly.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A supposed serpent, reptile, or worms in the belly that bite the ribs or cause the pain and yellowing associated with hunger.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: This is the pre-Islamic medical belief referred to in explanations of the expression لا صَفَرَ; the reported belief in its transmission from person to person was denied.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The intellect, understanding, heart, or inmost mind.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used in expressions for something that does not adhere to one’s mind or that one’s soul does not accept.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A contract, compact, covenant, surety, or responsibility.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A conventional nominal meaning synonymous with عَقْدٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Ṣafar, the second month of the Arabian calendar; also, in الصَّفَرَانِ, the pair of Muḥarram and Ṣafar.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The month-name has several traditional explanations connected with emptied houses, provisions, or travel and raiding.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yellowness or a known yellow color; the term can also be applied to blackness.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The color is described as less intense than red and may occur in animals, other things, or water.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A proper name for a she-goat.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A lexicalized proper-name use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Belonging to the early autumn or the transition from summer heat to cold; by extension, the offspring, rain, or plant growth associated with that period.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The seasonal boundaries vary among authorities; the term may denote the period itself, its rain, an autumn plant, or offspring of sheep and goats born then.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A yellow variety of dates from Yemen, dried while still in the state called بُسْر.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The dried dates crumble when rubbed and are used to sweeten or replace sugar in سَوِيق.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A sect of the Khārijites, also called a party of the Ḥarūriyya.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name has several reported derivations, including relation to a place, a leader, yellow complexions, or being void of religion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Mahālaba, a group celebrated for bounty and generosity.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A separate eponymous use of the same form, related to Abū Ṣufra.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A poor man; in the plural, poor men.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The final ت is described as augmentative.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The dry remains of the plant بُهْمَى, a barleygrass, or a related plant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Its name is associated with its yellow color; its prickles cling to horses’ lips.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A disease involving yellow fluid or water collecting in the abdomen and making the person yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The entry also gives a surgical description of the condition and identifies it with a related medical term in one account.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The yellowing of wheat before the grain has become full.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized agricultural use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Remains of straw or other fodder lodged at the roots of an animal’s teeth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A term for material left around the teeth of beasts.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A tick or similar small insect found in the solid hoofs or toes of camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The term may denote the tick itself or, according to one report, a small animalcule in that location.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Whistling or the sound produced by whistling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is also used in the modern language for sapphire, treated separately below.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Sapphire.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A later or contemporary lexical use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A plant or herbage that has withered and changed to yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The word denotes the altered plant material rather than yellow color in the abstract.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A dam or embankment between two tracts of land.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized geographical noun.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A species of bird that whistles.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The name is motivated by the bird’s call.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular small bird, identified with a صَعْوَةٌ or related passerine bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The form has variant pronunciation and spelling in the cited discussion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A kind of plant; alternatively, according to another lexical report, a kind of garment or cloth.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The two applications are reported as competing lexical explanations.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A maker or fabricator of brass vessels or brasswork.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A professional noun derived from the metal sense of صُفْرٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The entire quill of a feather.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized noun with a distinct vocalization from the occupational term صَفَّارٌ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A whistle or pipe, especially a hollow copper object used by a boy to whistle to pigeons or call an ass to drink.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun denotes the instrument, not merely the act of whistling.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The anus.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A dialectal use reported for the Sawād.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A whistler or one that whistles; also a bird that whistles, especially a nonpredatory or cowardly bird.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The bird application includes several reported identifications and is not limited to one species.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A thief or coward, conventionally associated with furtive whistling.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: In one explanation the whistling is directed to a woman for illicit intercourse; the source also uses the word for a cowardly person.

other_classical_meanings.definition: In مَا بِهَا صَافِرٌ, no one is in the house.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The expression literally refers to someone who whistles or someone to be called by whistling; the active form is interpreted as passive in this construction.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A greater or more habitual whistler, in a comparative expression.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A comparative or superlative use illustrated by أَصْفَرُ مِنْ بُلْبُلٍ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: More or most empty, void, or vacant.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: Used of a house that is especially devoid of good or of the Book of God.

other_classical_meanings.definition: The Greeks or Romans, especially their kings.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The ethnic name has several traditional explanations, including an ancestor’s complexion.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A pair of yellow or yellow-associated substances, variously identified as gold and saffron, wars and saffron, wars and gold, or saffron and raisins.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The exact pair varies among lexical authorities.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Gold.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A nominalized color term used for the precious metal.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Yellow bile, one of the bodily humors.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The noun is motivated by the bile’s color.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A bow made from the tree called نَبْع.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized nominal application of the form.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A female locust that is without eggs.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized zoological use.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A particular plant or herb of plains, soft ground, or sands, eaten eagerly by camels.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The plant is described as spreading along the ground and having leaves like lettuce.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A poor man.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A specialized active-participial noun distinct from the color adjective مُصْفَرّ.

other_classical_meanings.definition: A derogatory expression for a cowardly or effeminate, luxury-softened man; it is also explained as one who dyed his buttocks with saffron and practiced anal intercourse.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The sources dispute whether the expression derives from whistling or from dyeing yellow; both explanations are preserved because they yield the same conventional expression.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Those whose distinguishing ensign or sign is yellow.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: An appellation formed in parallel with names based on red or white insignia.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Hungry.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A passive-participial adjective associated with the empty or unfed state.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Of an animal, having the ear wholly cut away or being lean and emaciated, in terminology concerning animals forbidden for sacrifice.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: The authorities disagree over which of the related forms carries the severed-ear versus emaciated meaning.

other_classical_meanings.definition: Afflicted with ṣufār or discharging yellow fluid from the belly.
other_classical_meanings.usage_conditions: A medical passive-participial use.

cautions: The reading of صَفْرَاءُ as black in 2:69 is explicitly reported but disputed; yellow is the ordinary reading.
The Quranic صُفْرٌ in 77:33 is interpreted either as the plural adjective أَصْفَرٌ, with yellow or dark camel coloration, or as the metal noun صُفْرٌ; the alternatives should not be conflated.
The exact derivation and force of the expression مَصَفِّرُ اسْتِهِ are disputed in the Classical evidence, so its competing explanations are retained.
